title: Thanksgiving Traditions: Turkey, Races, and Football
summary:
Thanksgiving is full of fun traditions. It falls on the fourth Thursday of November. This year, that is November 26.

Long ago, in 1621, European settlers and Native Americans shared a harvest feast. The first feast probably had geese and ducks, but turkey became the star of the meal. Writer Sarah Josepha Hale helped make turkey popular.

Cranberry sauce is another favorite. Cookbook writer Amelia Simmons first said to serve it with roast turkey in 1796. Years later, General Ulysses S. Grant reportedly ordered it for soldiers in 1864.

Many people start the morning with a turkey trot, a fun race where runners wear costumes and raise money for charity. The oldest one began in Buffalo, New York, in 1896. Now it draws 14,000 runners each year.

At the White House, the president pardons a turkey, sparing it from dinner. This took its current form in 1989, when President George H.W. Bush pardoned a turkey. Its origin is unclear.

Football ends the day. The Detroit Lions first played on Thanksgiving in 1934. In 2025, the three games averaged 44.7 million viewers, a record.
why_it_matters: Thanksgiving is a holiday many kids celebrate with their families, so knowing where its traditions come from makes the day more fun to enjoy.

background_read: Thanksgiving is a holiday when families and friends gather to share a big meal and give thanks for what they have.
Many of its traditions, like eating turkey and cranberry sauce, grew from a harvest feast shared long ago.
Over time, new traditions were added, like morning races, the turkey pardon at the White House, and football games.
